title: The travels of Marco Polo (1271-1295)
subtitle: From Venice to the court of Kublai Khan and back

stop.title: Acre, the crusaders' last port
stop.story: Niccolò and Maffeo Polo take seventeen-year-old Marco with them from Venice. In Acre, the crusaders' last city, they call on the papal legate Tedaldo Visconti. Kublai Khan has asked them for oil from Jerusalem, so they go there first.

stop.title: Jerusalem, oil for the Khan
stop.story: Kublai Khan wants oil from the lamp that burns at the tomb of Christ in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. The Polos travel overland from Acre to Jerusalem to fetch it. It is a gift they will carry all the way to China.

stop.title: Back in Acre
stop.story: With the oil they return to Acre. Visconti gives them letters for the Khan. Later he hears that he himself has been elected pope, and he sends two friars after them, but the friars soon turn back.

stop.title: Ayas, the gateway inland
stop.story: Ayas (Lajazzo) in Lesser Armenia is a busy trading port. Spices and silk from the east arrive here, and here the Polos leave the sea to travel on overland.

stop.title: Tabriz, market of Persia
stop.story: Tabriz is a great trading city in the empire of the Mongol Ilkhans. Marco describes merchants from many lands and cloth of silk and gold.

stop.title: Hormuz, ships without nails
stop.story: In Hormuz the Polos want to take a ship to China. But the ships are sewn together with coconut-fibre rope, without iron nails. They think them too dangerous and travel on overland.

stop.title: Balkh, a ruined city
stop.story: Balkh was one of the oldest and richest cities of Central Asia. Marco still sees beautiful palaces, but also the destruction the Mongols left there.

stop.title: Over the roof of the world
stop.story: The travellers cross the high plain of the Pamir for twelve days. Marco writes that fire burns less brightly there and that wild sheep with enormous horns live there; those sheep now carry his name.

stop.title: Khotan, oasis of jade
stop.story: Khotan lies on the edge of the Taklamakan Desert. Its rivers carry jade down from the mountains, a stone that is worth more than gold in China.

stop.title: Ganzhou, a year of waiting
stop.story: After the deserts of Lop and the Gobi, the Polos reach Ganzhou. Marco says they stay here for about a year on their business.

stop.title: At the court of Kublai Khan
stop.story: After more than three years on the road, the Polos reach Kublai Khan, first at his summer palace Shangdu (Xanadu) and then in his capital Khanbaliq, today's Beijing. Marco stays in the Khan's service for seventeen years.

stop.title: Zaiton, the great port
stop.story: Hundreds of ships lie in Zaiton (Quanzhou). Here the Polos are finally allowed to go home: they escort Princess Kököchin, who is to be married in Persia.

stop.title: After two years at sea
stop.story: The fleet sails past Sumatra, Ceylon and India back to Hormuz. The voyage takes more than two years, and of the hundreds on board only a few arrive alive.

stop.title: The princess is delivered
stop.story: The Polos bring Princess Kököchin to the court of the Ilkhans in Persia. On the way they hear that Kublai Khan has died.

stop.title: Trebizond, robbed on the Black Sea
stop.story: In Trebizond on the Black Sea the Polos are robbed of part of what they carry. From here they go on by ship to Constantinople.

stop.title: Back in Venice
stop.story: After twenty-four years they are back in Venice. A few years later Marco is a prisoner in Genoa. There he tells his story to Rustichello of Pisa, who turns it into a book.
